npc.blockade_officer.flavor_text: This is the line. Past Luyten's Star is uncharted space - no patrols, no beacons, no backup. Turn back while you still can.
npc.demolitions_expert.flavor_text: Breach charges, cutting torches, doors that don't want to open. If the patrol captain vouched for you, then the work is off the books - understand?
step.mil_q1_report.completion_flavor: The requisition disappears into a file that officially does not exist. When the clearance comes through, search the Mercury caves beneath the old mining station. If the cache is still there, someone has been protecting the Incident's secrets for a very long time.
step.mil_q1_report.description: Report to the Militia Captain on Earth. He has an unofficial explanation for the material on Mars, and an official reason to deny he ever saw it. A requisition cache on Mercury holds the parts for a breach package. Prove the cache survived, and he will decide whether you are useful enough to trust.
step.mil_q1_report.dialogue.militia_capt: Good. You are on the books now - my private books, which means they can be burned. A patrol found this material during the Incident. We called it a wreck, then a weapons test, then nothing at all. The requisition cache on Mercury is what remains of the response. Bring me proof it survived, and I will show you how we planned to open the door.
step.mil_q1_report.ready_message: Clearance came through. Go to Mercury and recover the cache beneath the old mining station. Bring the sealed requisition back before the next patrol decides to clean up the evidence for us.
step.mil_q1_report.title: Report to the Captain
step.mil_q2_cache.completion_flavor: The cache held exactly what the requisition promised: one sealed package, scrubbed serials, and no explanation for why it was hidden. The blockade inspector is expecting your transponder. Take it there before the silence around it attracts the wrong attention.
step.mil_q2_cache.description: The requisition cache lies beneath the Mercury mining station, in a cave system absent from every public survey. Recover the sealed requisition, then carry it to the Luyten's Star blockade. The Captain wants the package inspected before it comes anywhere near the Mars door.
step.mil_q2_cache.dialogue.militia_capta: The cache is deep in the Mercury caves - a sealed requisition the official logs don't show. Everything the breach package needs is inside it. Secure it and bring it back.
step.mil_q2_cache.title: The Cache
step.mil_q3_inspection.completion_flavor: The blockade inspector signs off on every component. The serials are scrubbed, the seals are intact, and the requisition survives one more layer of questions. The Captain will contact you when the demolitions expert is prepared to take responsibility for the next step.
step.mil_q3_inspection.description: The requisition is in your hold under serial numbers that no longer exist. Deliver it to the blockade inspector at Luyten's Star. The route crosses pirate space and the edge of the mapped frontier; every jump is another chance for the package to be lost, seized, or noticed.
step.mil_q3_inspection.dialogue.blockade: Still carrying the requisition? The Captain's inspector is here at the northern checkpoint. Hand it over and I'll make the paperwork disappear.

The seals check out. The inspection report disappears into a routine supply transfer: no flags, no questions, and no record of why the Militia needed alien-grade hardware on the frontier. The Captain will contact you when the demolitions expert answers.

The Captain sent word. Scratched requisition, scrubbed serials - I know the drill. Hand it over. I'll log it as routine supply transfer, and no one asks questions. The Captain will call when the inspection clears.
step.mil_q3_inspection.dialogue.militia_: The blockade inspector is waiting at Luyten's Star's northern checkpoint. Hand over the requisition. He will log it as routine supply and keep the package buried under ordinary paperwork.
step.mil_q3_inspection.ready_message: The blockade has verified the package without learning what it is. Recruit the demolitions expert at Epsilon Eridani b. Use my name, not the requisition number. He is the last person in the Militia who still knows how to work on doors that were never designed to be breached.
step.mil_q3_inspection.title: The Inspection
step.mil_q4_demolitions.completion_flavo: The demolitions expert signs on. Tuning the charge to alien alloy will take time, and the test will need a target that can survive the first failure. The Captain will call when the prototype is ready.
step.mil_q4_demolitions.description: Recruit the demolitions expert at Epsilon Eridani b. The frontier colony's Militia building is the last place he still answers calls. Use the Captain's name; the breach package needs someone willing to admit what it is for.
step.mil_q4_demolitions.dialogue.demolit: The charge is ready for a live-fire test. The Captain has chosen a target at Cygni b: pirate captains, hard enough to stress the package and disposable enough that no official report will mourn the test. Ask him for the coordinates.

The Captain sent you, which means this job is either important or already a mistake. I build charges for structures that resist ordinary physics. If the requisition is genuine, I can tune one to the Mars door. But understand this: a successful breach tells you nothing about what is waiting on the other side.
step.mil_q4_demolitions.ready_message: The prototype is calibrated. Clear the pirate captains at Cygni b and bring back the combat data. The Captain wants a live-fire test before the charge touches the Mars door; the first failure must happen somewhere we can survive it.
step.mil_q4_demolitions.title: The Expert
step.mil_q5_livefire.completion_flavor: The prototype held under fire. The test report contains one useful answer and several new questions: the charge couples to the alien material instead of simply breaking it. The Captain is assembling the final package.
step.mil_q5_livefire.description: The breach charge is built, but a laboratory result is not proof. Take the prototype to Cygni b and put it through a live-fire test against five pirate captains. If it fails there, it fails on Mars. If it works, we still have to decide whether opening the door is wiser than leaving it sealed.
step.mil_q5_livefire.dialogue.militia_ca: The charge needs a real stress-test before it touches Mars. Five pirate captains at Cygni b will serve as the target. We are mounting the prototype to your ship; fire it, record the result, and do not mistake a successful detonation for a successful containment plan.
step.mil_q5_livefire.ready_message: The final breach package is assembled. Report to the Captain on Earth. Once it is in your hands, the Militia can no longer pretend this is only an investigation.
step.mil_q5_livefire.title: Live-Fire Test
step.mil_q6_charge.description: Return to the Militia Captain on Earth. The breach package is tuned, tested, and ready to open the alien seal on Mars. The Captain wants the operation contained from the first jump to the last.
step.mil_q6_charge.dialogue.militia_capt: There it is. Tuned to the same material that ended the Incident. Take it to Mars and open the door. We contain whatever is inside, we preserve what can be learned, and we tell no one until we know which of those tasks is still possible. That is the order. The door is not.
step.mil_q6_charge.title: The Charge
